answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with an escalating registration burn tied to funding provenance. Every new identity must burn a small fee before acting; identities funded from the same wallet face a fee that rises with each further registration from that source. One honest agent pays once, a walnut-sized cost, while a farmer minting hollow copies watches the price climb until no haven of cheap identities remains. Since the burn follows funding, not names, renaming fakes cannot reset it, and mass forgery turns ruinous before buying influence.
